platforms.name: DJI Air 3S
platforms.description:
Copy this template for every mission.
**IM SAFE**

- Illness	Am I sick or feeling unwell?
- Medication	Am I on any medications that impair judgment?
- Stress	Am I under significant stress?
- Alcohol	Have I consumed alcohol in the last 8 hours?
- Fatigue	Am I rested and alert?
- Emotion	Am I emotionally stable and focused?

items.text: Review NOTAMs, TFRs, and local airspace status (e.g., through B4UFLY, Airdata, or LAANC app) for every planned flight location.
Obtain LAANC airspace or any other required operational approvals; save/screenshot reference number.
Verify drone registration, operator license, REC or Part 107 certificate, and proof of insurance coverage.
Review and print/prepare documentation as required (insurance, waivers, permits, flight authorizations).
Confirm scheduled mission details and participants; notify property owners, team, or relevant authorities of planned activity.
Confirm mission deliverables: photos, video, thermal, mapping, inspection shots, Matterport, client-specific views.
Confirm firmware/software compatibility before leaving; avoid field updates unless required.
Review and finalize flight plan, RTH/”fail safe” parameters, and designated landing/takeoff zones.
Check local weather forecast for flight session (visibility, wind, precipitation, extreme temperatures); note alternate or “no-go” windows.
Record weather METAR/TAF for historical tracking in Dronelogbook/mission log.
Ensure batteries (drone, controller, tablets/devices) are charged at ≥75%.
Check battery condition (no bulging, damage, or swelling); review battery log for cycles/performance issues.
Inspect drone body, arms, landing gear, and propellers for cracks, chips, or debris.
Secure propellers and payload (gimbal, camera, sensor) and remove any transit covers.
Perform office power/connectivity check: controller/display, aircraft, app, SD/storage, camera feed, and battery status.
Insert SD card or memory device with adequate free space for mission.
Confirm SD card/storage has been formatted or cleared after backup.
Confirm aircraft, controller, tablet, and app can connect before departure.
Confirm required field kit is packed: landing pad, cones/signs, PPE, fire extinguisher, radio, chargers, spare props, tools.
Shut down in proper sequence and pack aircraft, batteries, controller, tablet, payload, SD cards, and field kit securely.
Confirm visual line-of-sight, clear takeoff/landing areas (minimum 25 ft. free radius), identify emergency recovery zones.
Remove gimbal cover
Power up remote, display device, and then aircraft (in recommended sequence).
Confirm no firmware/software incompatibility warnings before flight. (Dronelogbook log update).
Verify RTH altitude set above highest local obstacle; set home point to accurate location (controller/app).
Calibrate compass, IMU, and gimbal only if requested by app, abnormal behavior is observed, or operating conditions require it.
Confirm GPS lock with sufficient satellites and green status on controller/app.
Check all sensors, IMU, obstacle avoidance, and transmission signal strength.
Test camera FPV (live transmission, calibration, and lens cleaning).
Review all error messages, and confirm “no warnings” state.
Confirm site access and notify property owner/client/contact as needed.
Conduct site hazard scan: people, vehicles, animals, trees, wires, towers, terrain, reflective surfaces, water, dust, loose debris.
Identify emergency landing / recovery zones.
Confirm takeoff/landing zone is stable, level, and clear of loose debris.
Unfold arms and verify arms are locked.
Verify motor mounts are secure.
Verify propellers are correct, undamaged, properly seated, and tightened.
Verify payload/gimbal/camera/sensor is secure.
Clean lens, camera, thermal sensor, obstacle sensors, and lights as needed.
Confirm home point is accurate.
Confirm geofence, max altitude, max distance, RTH, low-battery, and failsafe settings.
Confirm aircraft status is green/ready.
Brief all team members on mission plan, emergency/abort procedures, and assign roles.
Review and verify waypoints/uploaded mission data for autonomous flights (if applicable).
Confirm DroneLogbook logging is active or ready before launch.
Set up warning signs and secure launch & control area
Don safety vests, eyewear, and helmets.
Make sure Lithium fire extinguisher is on site and current.
Make sure aviation radio is scanning the local frequencies.
Complete IM SAFE self-check: Illness, Medication, Stress, Alcohol, Fatigue, Emotion.
Confirm RPIC and visual observer roles if more than one person is present.
Brief client/bystanders on safe distance and no-entry area if applicable.
Review planned altitude, flight path, duration, and mission objective.
Review communication callouts: “Spooling Motors,” “Taking Off,” “Landing,” “Lost Link,” “RTH Activated.”
Confirm max altitude, max distance, geofence, RTH, low-battery, and failsafe settings.
Confirm automated waypoint mission is loaded, reviewed, and matches the intended site.
Confirm abort/mission pause procedure for autonomous flights.
Confirm nearby aviation frequency monitoring is required or not required for this site.
Last visual scan for hazards, bystanders, and overhead obstacles.
Set flight mode (P/N/S), failsafe behavior, RTH settings, and abort procedure.
Begin flight log/record in Airdata UAV and/or Dronelogbook.
Start motors, perform short hover test (check for abnormal noise/vibration), verify full telemetry (battery, satellites, camera, GPS, transmission).
Confirm “Ready for Flight” via checklist, and commence mission.
Confirm weather still remains within mission limits.
Confirm battery level and estimated mission time are sufficient.
Confirm controller signal, GPS, camera feed, storage, and telemetry are normal.
Announce: “Spooling Motors.”
Start motors and verify normal sound/propeller behavior.
Announce: “Taking Off.”
Take off and climb to approximately 10 feet.
Perform control check: yaw, pitch, roll, climb, descend.
Confirm aircraft is stable with no abnormal vibration, drift, warnings, or control issues.
Commence mission.
Maintain visual line of sight.
Continuously scan airspace and ground for aircraft, birds, people, vehicles, wires, and changing hazards.
Monitor battery percentage, voltage behavior, and remaining flight time.
Monitor GPS, IMU, compass, control link, and transmission strength.
Monitor wind, gusts, and aircraft behavior.
Monitor nearby aviation frequencies if applicable.
Confirm required photos/video/thermal/mapping/inspection data are being captured.
Pause or abort mission if aircraft, environment, people, or data quality becomes unsafe/unacceptable.
Complete planned mission.
Return aircraft to landing area with adequate battery reserve.
Hover around 10 feet and orient aircraft away from RPIC/crew where practical.
Confirm landing area is clear.
Announce: “Landing.”
Descend smoothly while maintaining aircraft over landing zone.
Once aircraft touches down, reduce throttle to zero; do not manipulate other controls.
Disarm aircraft.
Announce: “Disarmed.”
Power off aircraft.
Remove aircraft from landing pad.
Install gimbal/camera cover as appropriate.
Remove propellers if applicable.
Power off controller.
Power off tablet/mobile device.
Secure aircraft, batteries, SD cards, and field kit.
Inspect aircraft, props, motors, gimbal, camera, sensors, and landing gear for damage or debris.
Check battery temperature and condition after flight.
Mark batteries used and record cycle/performance notes if needed.
Confirm photos/video/mission data were captured before leaving site.
Back up SD card / mission data as soon as practical.
Upload or sync logs to Airdata UAV and/or DroneLogbook.
Record actual flight time, location, weather, crew, aircraft, battery IDs, and anomalies.
Document incidents, near misses, client issues, or maintenance needs.
Recharge batteries according to storage/next-mission requirements.
Reset kit for next mission.
Announce: “Lost Link.”
Verify RTH behavior if automatic RTH initiates.
Activate RTH if appropriate and not already triggered.
Monitor aircraft direction, altitude, and speed.
Confirm landing area is clear.
Announce: “Returning to Home.”
Announce: “Landing.”
Wait until aircraft lands and disarms.
Announce: “Disarmed.”
Power down aircraft.
Investigate interference, controller/app errors, antenna orientation, and C2 issues.

platforms.name: Parrot ANAFI USA
platforms.description: Copy this template for every mission

items.text: Review NOTAMs, TFRs, and local airspace status for every planned flight location.
Obtain LAANC airspace authorization or other required operational approvals; save/screenshot reference number.
Verify drone registration, Remote ID status if applicable, Part 107 certificate, and proof of insurance coverage.
Review and prepare documentation: insurance, waivers, permits, flight authorizations, site access notes.
Confirm scheduled mission details, location, client/contact, crew, and participants.
Notify property owner, client, team, or relevant authorities of planned activity as needed.
Confirm mission deliverables: visual photos, video, thermal imagery, zoom inspection, mapping, facility shots, client-specific views.
Confirm ANAFI USA GOV, Skycontroller USA, FreeFlight 6 USA, and batteries are assigned for this mission.
Confirm firmware/software compatibility before leaving; avoid field updates unless required.
If operating offline, confirm required FreeFlight 6 USA APK/update files are available if needed.
Review and finalize flight plan, launch area, landing area, emergency recovery zones, RTH behavior, and failsafe assumptions.
Confirm whether automated/assisted flight modes will be used.
If using automated/assisted flight modes, confirm GPS availability is expected and the mission starts from a wide open area.
Check local weather forecast: wind, gusts, visibility, precipitation, lightning, temperature, and no-go windows.
Record METAR/TAF or weather source for DroneLogbook/mission log.
Ensure ANAFI USA batteries, Skycontroller USA, tablet/display, phone, and backup devices are charged.
Check ANAFI USA battery condition: no swelling, cracks, damage, moisture, or abnormal behavior.
Confirm ANAFI USA batteries are awake from storage/wintering mode and fully charged if they have been unused for an extended period.
Inspect aircraft body, arms, motor mounts, landing feet, gimbal, camera, thermal sensor, vertical camera, ultrasonic sensor, and propellers.
Confirm propellers are intact, correctly installed, free to rotate, and fully screwed on.
Confirm no unauthorized accessories/add-ons are attached that could affect weight, communications, motors, or center of gravity.
Confirm microSD card is inserted, compatible, formatted/cleared after backup, and has adequate free space.
Confirm FDR/log file preservation process if an incident occurs.
Perform office power/connectivity check: Skycontroller USA, FreeFlight 6 USA, aircraft, microSD/storage, camera feed, thermal feed, battery status.
Confirm Skycontroller USA and ANAFI USA are paired.
Confirm required field kit is packed: landing pad, cones/signs, PPE, lithium fire extinguisher, aviation radio, chargers, spare props, tools, USB cables, cleaning cloth, tablet shade.
Shut down in proper sequence and pack aircraft, batteries, Skycontroller USA, tablet, SD cards, and field kit securely.
Confirm site access and notify property owner/client/contact upon arrival if needed.
Conduct site hazard scan: people, vehicles, animals, birds, trees, wires, towers, terrain, water, reflective surfaces, dust, loose debris, metal structures, and RF interference sources.
Confirm visual line of sight can be maintained throughout the mission.
Confirm takeoff/landing zone is stable, level, clear, and at least 25 ft. free radius where practical.
Identify emergency landing/recovery zones.
Set up launch/control area with cones, signs, or safety perimeter as needed.
Don PPE: safety vest, eye protection, helmet if required.
Confirm lithium fire extinguisher is on site and current.
Turn on aviation radio / monitor nearby airport frequencies if applicable.
Position ANAFI USA on a flat, even, clear surface.
Remove gimbal protective cover.
Unfold ANAFI USA arms and verify arms are locked.
Verify propellers are correct, undamaged, properly installed, free, and fully screwed on.
Verify ANAFI USA battery is seated and all battery hooks are engaged.
Power on Skycontroller USA.
Confirm FreeFlight 6 USA launches properly on Skycontroller USA.
Power on ANAFI USA by holding aircraft power button.
Confirm Skycontroller USA and ANAFI USA connect successfully.
Confirm microSD card is recognized and available storage is sufficient.
Confirm aircraft, Skycontroller USA, and FreeFlight 6 USA show no required update or incompatibility warning.
Confirm aircraft status is ready/green.
Confirm GPS synchronization if flying outdoors, at night, or using automated/assisted flight modes.
If flying without GPS, confirm ground texture and lighting are sufficient for optical flow/vertical camera stabilization.
Confirm home point / precise home status if available.
Confirm RTH height is appropriate for the site and above highest local obstacle.
Confirm max altitude, max distance, geofence, RTH, low-battery Smart RTH, and failsafe settings.
Calibrate ANAFI USA, Skycontroller USA, magnetometer, gimbal, camera, or thermal sensor only if requested by FreeFlight 6 USA or required by observed behavior.
Confirm thermal calibration status if using thermal imaging.
Confirm camera/gimbal status and horizon alignment.
Clean lens, thermal sensor, vertical camera, ultrasonic sensor, lights, and exposed surfaces as needed.
Test visual camera feed.
Test thermal camera feed.
Test zoom/inspection view if mission requires it.
Confirm Skycontroller antennas are oriented toward ANAFI USA and expected C2/Wi-Fi link path is clear.
Review all error messages and confirm no unresolved warnings.
Complete IM SAFE self-check.
Confirm RPIC.
Confirm visual observer role if more than one person is present.
Brief all crew on mission plan, operating area, altitude, duration, emergency/abort procedures, and roles.
Brief client/bystanders on safe distance and no-entry area if applicable.
Review planned flight path, inspection targets, photo/video/thermal requirements, and mission objective.
Review communication callouts: “Spooling Motors,” “Taking Off,” “Landing,” “Lost Link,” “RTH Activated,” “Emergency Landing.”
Confirm DroneLogbook logging is active or ready before launch.
Confirm Airdata or other telemetry/logging workflow if used.
Review and verify waypoints/uploaded mission data for autonomous flights if applicable.
Confirm automated/assisted mission starts and ends from a wide open area when practical.
Confirm abort/mission pause procedure for automated/assisted flights.
Confirm nearby aviation frequency monitoring is required or not required for this site.
Confirm privacy, data handling, and client-sensitive capture boundaries.
Confirm no one is within unsafe proximity of the aircraft or launch zone.
Final scan for hazards, bystanders, animals, vehicles, aircraft, wires, towers, and overhead obstacles.
Confirm weather remains within mission limits.
Confirm battery level and estimated mission time are sufficient.
Confirm Skycontroller USA battery level is sufficient.
Confirm aircraft battery is locked, healthy, and sufficient.
Confirm controller signal / Wi-Fi link is good.
Confirm GPS, camera feed, thermal feed, storage, telemetry, and aircraft status are normal.
Confirm RTH height, home point, low-battery Smart RTH, and failsafe behavior.
Confirm takeoff area is clear.
Announce: “Spooling Motors.”
Press Take-off/Land or initiate takeoff through FreeFlight 6 USA as appropriate.
Announce: “Taking Off.”
Climb to approximately 10 feet.
Perform hover check for abnormal noise, vibration, drift, warnings, or control issues.
Perform control check: yaw, pitch, roll, climb, descend.
Confirm camera/gimbal/thermal feed remains stable.
Confirm aircraft stable and telemetry normal.
Commence mission.
Maintain visual line of sight unless specifically authorized otherwise.
Continuously scan airspace and ground for aircraft, birds, people, vehicles, wires, and changing hazards.
Monitor ANAFI USA battery level, remaining flight time, and Smart RTH alerts.
Monitor Skycontroller USA battery level.
Monitor Wi-Fi/C2 link strength and antenna orientation.
Monitor GPS, magnetometer/compass, IMU, and aircraft behavior.
Monitor wind, gusts, drift, and aircraft stability.
Monitor nearby aviation frequencies if applicable.
Confirm required photos/video/thermal/zoom/inspection data are being captured.
Confirm thermal images are usable and recalibrate thermal if needed.
Confirm gimbal/camera horizon remains acceptable.
Pause or abort mission if aircraft, environment, people, battery, C2 link, or data quality becomes unsafe/unacceptable.
Complete planned mission.
Return aircraft to landing area with adequate battery reserve.
Hover around 10 feet and orient aircraft away from RPIC/crew where practical.
Confirm landing area is clear.
Announce: “Landing.”
Descend smoothly while maintaining aircraft over landing zone.
Once aircraft touches down, allow aircraft to settle.
Disarm/stop motors.
Announce: “Disarmed.”
Power off ANAFI USA.
Remove aircraft from landing pad.
Install gimbal protective cover.
Inspect propellers before handling/packing.
Power off Skycontroller USA.
Secure aircraft, batteries, microSD card, Skycontroller USA, and field kit.
Keep used batteries separated/identified for post-flight logging.
Inspect aircraft body, arms, motor mounts, propellers, gimbal, visual camera, thermal sensor, vertical camera, ultrasonic sensor, and landing feet.
Check battery temperature and condition after flight.
Mark batteries used and record cycle/performance notes if needed.
Confirm photos/video/thermal/mission data were captured before leaving site.
Confirm client-required shots/views were completed.
Back up microSD card / mission data as soon as practical.
Preserve FDR folder if there was a crash, abnormal event, error, or incident.
Upload or sync logs to DroneLogbook and/or Airdata as applicable.
Record actual flight time, location, weather, crew, aircraft, battery IDs, anomalies, and maintenance notes.
Document incidents, near misses, client issues, unsafe conditions, or maintenance needs.
Recharge batteries according to next-mission/storage requirements.
Clean aircraft, sensors, case, and field kit.
Reset kit for next mission.

checklists.name: Emergency Procedures: Lost Link / C2 Link Degradation

items.text: Announce: “Lost Link” or “Weak Link.”
Confirm antenna orientation toward ANAFI USA.
Stop unnecessary aircraft movement if control remains available.
Verify RTH behavior if automatic RTH initiates.
Activate RTH manually if appropriate and not already triggered.
Monitor aircraft direction, altitude, and speed.
Confirm landing area is clear.
Announce: “Returning to Home.”
Regain manual control if safe and appropriate.
Announce: “Landing.”
Land and disarm.
Power down aircraft.
Announce: “Lost Link” or “Weak Link.”
Confirm antenna orientation toward ANAFI USA.
Stop unnecessary aircraft movement if control remains available.
Verify RTH behavior if automatic RTH initiates.
Activate RTH manually if appropriate and not already triggered.
Monitor aircraft direction, altitude, and speed.
Confirm landing area is clear.
Announce: “Returning to Home.”
Regain manual control if safe and appropriate.
Announce: “Landing.”
Land and disarm.
Power down aircraft.
Announce: “Uncommanded Input.”
Attempt to stabilize aircraft.
Stop mission and climb/hold if safe.
Return manually if able.
Activate RTH only if GPS/home point are reliable and RTH path is safe.
Land as soon as safely possible.
Announce: “Landing.”
Disarm.
Power down.
Inspect aircraft, propellers, gimbal, sensors, and battery.
Do not relaunch until issue is understood and resolved.

checklists.name: Emergency Procedures: Loss of GPS / Poor GPS

items.text: Announce: “GPS Issue.”
Maintain manual control.
Avoid automated/assisted flight modes.
Do not rely on RTH if home point/GPS is unreliable.
Confirm adequate ground texture and lighting for optical-flow stabilization.
Return manually and land as soon as safely possible.
Confirm landing area is clear.
Announce: “Landing.”
Disarm and power down.
Troubleshoot GPS/magnetometer interference.
Check environment for metal structures, vehicles, rebar, towers, or electromagnetic interference.
Announce: “Lost Visual.”
Stop lateral movement if safe.
Use camera/map orientation to assist recovery.
Visual observer attempts to reacquire aircraft if present.
If unable to regain VLOS, verify GPS/home point and initiate RTH if safe.
Follow RTH checklist.
Land as soon as safely practical.

checklists.name: Emergency Procedures: Smart RTH / Manual RTH

items.text: Announce: “RTH Activated.”
Confirm RTH altitude is safe for the site.
Monitor aircraft return path.
Confirm landing area is clear.
Be ready to regain manual control if unsafe conditions develop.
Pause/cancel RTH only if manual control is available and safe.
Land aircraft.
Announce: “Disarmed.”
